claims.text: Traditional EAM references have inadequate phase-space overlap with ab initio multicomponent HEA liquids.
Traditional EAM references produce large thermodynamic-integration path mismatches for HEA liquids.
An MLIP trained on an expanded ab initio liquid dataset should replace the EAM reference in thermodynamic-integration calculations.
The MLIP training dataset should contain a wide diversity of high-temperature liquid atomic configurations.
MLIPs inherently account for many-body interactions that are not captured by EAM potentials.
MLIPs can represent subtle structural fluctuations that are not captured by EAM potentials.
Training on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture the complex many-body effects of HEA liquids.
Training on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations enables the MLIP to capture rapid structural fluctuations in HEA liquids.
Improved representation of local atomic environments will increase overlap between the MLIP reference and ab initio target configuration spaces.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The MLIP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
MLIP-referenced thermodynamic integration will yield free-energy estimates that converge more closely to full ab initio results than EAM-referenced calculations.
The proposed method applies to HEAs containing at least five principal elements in near-equimolar ratios.
The proposed method applies to solid and predominantly liquid HEA states at approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
The expected benefits may not occur outside the specified temperature or composition range.
The expected benefits may not occur when the ab initio training dataset is insufficiently diverse.
